content.text:
Hold scoped promotion for two concrete issues: stale output-parser state across reconnect, and an output/disconnection ordering race.

1. **Reconnect can make valid MIDI fail capture.** [native.py:214](/home/andy/projects/monome-emulator-midi-hotplug/src/runtime/native.py:214) resets `midi_inputs`, but leaves `capture.decoders` intact. After an echoed SysEx chunk `[240,1,2]`, disconnect/reconnect followed by `[144,67,101]` raises `midi_sysex: Status interrupted an exclusive message` in [the capture decoder](/home/andy/projects/monome-emulator-midi-hotplug/src/devices/midi/__init__.py:30). I reproduced that decoder failure without modifying files. The [native probes:60](/home/andy/projects/monome-emulator-midi-hotplug/tests/midi_hotplug_native.py:60) use only `[240,1]` before removal—too short for norns to emit its first three-byte SysEx chunk—so they miss this lifecycle case. **Fix:** reset the affected output decoder at the ordered connection boundary, preserving raw history, sequence accounting and outstanding notes. Add a native case that disconnects after an emitted SysEx chunk and verifies fresh MIDI after reconnect.

2. **The atomic connected flag does not serialize output with removal.** [prepare_midi_hotplug.py:34](/home/andy/projects/monome-emulator-midi-hotplug/scripts/prepare_midi_hotplug.py:34) inserts a connected-state check before output emission, but that send path never takes `midi_connection_lock`. Meanwhile [lines 51 onward](/home/andy/projects/monome-emulator-midi-hotplug/scripts/prepare_midi_hotplug.py:51) change state and emit transition metadata under that lock. A Lua send can pass the check, be descheduled, then emit after the device thread records disconnection. Both generated candidates contain this interleaving. **Fix:** serialize the connected check through emission with the transition boundary, using consistent lock ordering. Add a focused concurrent-send/removal probe; the existing retained-send test runs after removal acknowledgement and cannot expose this race.

The 10 connection/drop tests and five schedule-evidence tests pass. Both candidate patch/source hashes and all three recorded hot-plug run artifact ledgers match their recorded hashes.

**CONFIDENCE: High.** The capture failure was reproduced at decoder level; the race follows from source ordering, but neither new case was exercised in a fresh native run during this read-only review.
